claims.statement: The service layer is nine interfaces in com.caozhihu.tmall.service that all extend BaseService, plus nine implementations in com.caozhihu.tmall.service.impl that extend BaseServiceImpl (which itself implements BaseService and extends ServiceDelegateDAO); the implementations add only domain-specific methods, so all CRUD, paging and counting behaviour is inherited rather than written per entity.

BaseServiceImpl derives its entity class in the base constructor by throwing and catching an Exception purely to get a stack trace, reading getStackTrace()[1] as the instantiating subclass, Class.forName-ing it, stripping the "ServiceImpl" suffix via regex replaceAll to get the entity simple name, rewriting the package with replaceAll(".service.impl", ".pojo"), and Class.forName-ing the result into protected Class clazz.

The clazz derivation hard-codes a naming contract with no compiler or startup check: the implementation must live in a package ending .service.impl, the entity must exist in the sibling .pojo package under the matching simple name, and the subclass constructor must be frame 1 of the stack; when Class.forName fails, the ClassNotFoundException is only printed and construction succeeds with clazz == null, so the context still loads and the failure surfaces in the first list/total/get(int) call that uses clazz.

Descending id is the layer-wide default ordering: list(), listByPage(Page), listByParent(Object), list(Page, Object) and list(Object...) all build DetachedCriteria.forClass(clazz) and add Order.desc("id"); ProductServiceImpl.search is the only read that omits the ordering while adding a LIKE restriction on name.

Counting is done with HQL strings rather than criteria: total() runs "select count(*) from <clazz fully qualified name>" and total(Object parent) runs "select count(*) from <entity FQN> bean where bean.<uncapitalized parent simple name> = ?0" binding the parent entity, with PropertyServiceImpl.total(Category) hand-copying the same shape; the count and the paged rows are consequently two independent statements.

listByParent(Object) and list(Page, Object) build their restriction from the runtime parent argument's class simple name uncapitalized, so the query only works because every child entity names its association property exactly like the parent class (OrderItem.order, Product.category, Review.product, PropertyValue.product, Property.category); renaming a parent class without renaming the property silently changes or breaks the query.

list(Object... pairParams) folds key/value pairs into a HashMap and emits Restrictions.isNull(key) for null values and Restrictions.eq(key, value) otherwise, then adds Order.desc("id"); the null-means-IS NULL rule is what expresses a cart line (order is null), and the implementation fails at runtime for an odd argument count (ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException) or a null key (NullPointerException on toString()).

ServiceDelegateDAO holds the single DAO bean through the string-keyed @Resource(name = "dao") and forwards the whole HibernateTemplate API to it one-for-one (roughly a hundred one-line methods), so subclasses such as BaseServiceImpl call findByCriteria, save, get and delete without ever naming dao; an in-file comment records that @Autowired injected null on that field where @Resource worked.

ServiceDelegateDAO also injects the SessionFactory itself with @Resource(name = "sf") and pushes it into the DAOImpl bean a second time (DAOImpl already injects sf on its own setter), and it exposes getSessionFactory() as a pure forwarder; no service, action or interceptor opens a Hibernate session directly.

Each concrete service carries an explicit @Service("<name>Service") name while BaseServiceImpl carries a bare @Service, but since every consumer injects by type through @Autowired on interface fields, no service bean name is referenced by string — unlike the dao and sf names, which are load-bearing in ServiceDelegateDAO.

Single-entity writes are transactional because ServiceDelegateDAO declares @Transactional(readOnly = false) on save, update, delete and saveOrUpdate, and those declarations are inherited by every service — including the update and delete that BaseServiceImpl never overrides.

BaseServiceImpl.save overrides the inherited save and declares its own @Transactional, so a save call takes its transaction attributes from this override rather than from ServiceDelegateDAO.save; it also casts the returned Serializable key to Integer, which is valid only while every entity's @Id remains a primitive int.

The only multi-entity flows declare their own boundary with @Transactional(propagation = REQUIRED, rollbackForClassName = "Exception"): OrderServiceImpl.createOrder (Order insert plus one orderItemService.update per OrderItem) and ReviewServiceImpl.saveReviewAndUpdateOrderStatus (orderService.update plus the Review insert); the save/update self-calls inside them do not open new transactions, so the outer annotation is what makes the composite operation atomic.

PropertyValueServiceImpl.init is the third annotated service method (@Transactional(readOnly = false)); it reads the parent's Property rows, looks each one up together with the Product via list("property", property, "product", product), and inserts the missing PropertyValue rows inside one transaction.

Reads and in-memory enrichment helpers (list*, total*, get, OrderItemServiceImpl.fill, ProductImageServiceImpl.setFirstProductImage, ProductServiceImpl.setSaleAndReviewNumber) carry no @Transactional at all, and the layer mixes two write-annotation styles — bare @Transactional on BaseServiceImpl.save versus @Transactional(readOnly = false) on ServiceDelegateDAO — so the read-side boundary convention is left implicit.

OrderService exports six status constants (waitPay, waitDelivery, waitConfirm, waitReview, finish, delete) that are the cross-layer vocabulary for the plain String column Order.status: actions write them, Order.getStatusDesc() switches over them from inside the entity (so the pojo imports the service interface), and OrderServiceImpl.listByUserWithoutDelete filters them with Restrictions.ne("status", OrderService.delete) while adding no ordering.

ProductImageService exports type_single and type_detail, which are stored in the unconstrained ProductImage.type field and used both as list(...) criteria values and in views (a hidden field in web/admin/listProductImage.jsp writes the literal "type_single"), so the constant values and not just their names are part of the contract.
Because the inherited methods carry no entity type, the layer cannot detect a mis-routed call: ProductImageAction.delete deletes a ProductImage through propertyService, and the deletion succeeds.

PropertyServiceImpl redeclares list(Page, Category) and total(Category), which overload rather than override BaseServiceImpl's Object-typed methods, so which implementation runs depends on the caller's static type; a subclass cannot repoint the CRUD methods at a different entity because clazz is assigned only in the base constructor.

ProductServiceImpl.setSaleAndReviewNumber sums sale counts in Java over orderItemService.list("product", product) because the generic orderItemService.total(product) counts OrderItem rows rather than units; the replaced call and the reasoning remain in the file as comments, and the review count still uses the generic total().

No test exercises the service layer: TestTmall autowires DAOImpl and builds its own DetachedCriteria, so the only incidental coverage of the clazz derivation is that loading applicationContext.xml instantiates the nine service beans, and a naming violation would print ClassNotFoundException traces while both tests still pass.
